description: Local NASA LOLA terrain and NASA/JPL Horizons demonstration; 2026-11-01 through 2026-12-01 UTC.

sites.name: Connecting ridge

regionBoundsM.projection: South polar stereographic, radius 1737400m, central meridian 0 degrees

sites.description: Demonstration high-ground sample within NASA PGDA Site01; not an approved landing point.

terrain.coordinateFrame: Grid bounds are east/north great-circle arc offsets. Rows run north to south. GLB x=east, y=up, z=south in local tangent frame, including spherical curvature; no vertical exaggeration.
terrain.heightReference: heightsM are absolute radial surface elevations in meters relative to a 1737400m sphere, not local mesh y coordinates.

provenance.title: NASA LOLA 5 m Site01 DEM
provenance.detail: Surface heights in meters above 1737.4 km reference sphere; DE421 mean-Earth frame.

provenance.title: NASA PDS 80 m south-polar LOLA topography
provenance.detail: Native 80 m signed half-meter PDS product; heights relative to 1737.4 km reference radius.

provenance.title: PDS DEM scaling and projection label
NASA/JPL Horizons
provenance.detail: Airless apparent Sun/Earth center azimuth and elevation from coord@301; observer height includes DEM surface elevation.

limitations: Sample point chosen from a high 1.6 km-bin mean of the native 80 m DEM within the central half of a named NASA region; not a NASA-approved landing coordinate.
Horizon is sampled every 1 degree in azimuth and to 200 km range; narrow ridges between rays may be missed.
Near terrain uses 5 m source data; far terrain uses an 80 m grid and may underestimate narrow peaks.
Sun and Earth center visibility only; not a confirmed ground-station radio link or electrical-power estimate.
Hourly time sampling limits event timing; verify and refine near horizon crossings.
NASA's documented lunar mean-Earth coordinate convention is used; independent alignment checks and elevation uncertainty propagation remain future validation work.
The local 3D mesh is resampled to 125 m spacing and only spans 8 km; the horizon profile uses terrain out to 200 km.

horizon.method: Spherical line-of-sight, 2 m observer; 5 m near-field DEM, native 80 m far-field terrain; 1 degree bearing sampling.
